title: Stephen's speech (Acts 6:8–7:53)
hookLine: Stephen retells Israel's story from Abraham, with a face like an angel
carry: the most high dwells not in temples
tomorrow: the speech ends sharply. how does the room answer Stephen?

cards: Ask someone what they believe and the truest answer is sometimes a story, not a list. Stephen, one of the seven chosen to serve tables, is brought before the council, accused of speaking against the temple and the law.
Everyone there "saw his face as it had been the face of an angel." Why answer with a story? Because he's asked to explain himself, and his answer is his people's whole history, starting with Abraham.

teach.b: He begins: "Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia." Our father. Stephen is a Jew speaking to fellow Jews about their shared family.
Then he walks the story forward. Abraham, called out of his country.

teach.h: GOD IN EGYPT, IN THE DESERT.
teach.b: Joseph, sold into Egypt by his brothers, "but God was with him." Moses, a stranger in Midian, meeting God in a flame of fire in a bush in the desert. Notice where God keeps showing up: Mesopotamia, Egypt, the wilderness.

Then the building: "Solomon built him an house." And the line he's been walking toward: "Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands." One to tell a friend tonight: the idea isn't Stephen's invention.
He backs it with Isaiah, from Israel's own scriptures: "Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build me?"

teach.h: THE MOST HIGH DWELLS NOT IN TEMPLES.
teach.b: The speech ends sharply; he turns and accuses his hearers of resisting God, as he says their fathers did. What happens next is the next lesson.

how: Some churches keep a feast day for Saint Stephen soon after Christmas and remember him as a deacon and martyr; Acts 7 is read in some churches in the Easter season.

games.q: at a job interview they say, "tell us about yourself." you have a list of skills ready, and a story about how you got here. what's Stephen's way?
o: tell the story: where you started, and what kept showing up.
read the list, so you don't leave anything out.
keep it short, and let your work speak for you.
games.why: asked to explain himself, Stephen didn't list beliefs. he told a family story, starting with where: our father Abraham, in Mesopotamia.

practice: In three short sentences, said quietly out loud, tell where you've noticed something larger than you show up: a place, a person, a moment. Begin with where, the way Stephen began with Mesopotamia.
Then rest in the quiet after the last sentence.

wordCard.voice: Stephen's speech. Asked to defend himself, Stephen tells his people's story, where God keeps showing up far from home.
